messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx and timeouts for /v1/generate across region-us-west-2. Paging oncall now. Investigate: batching/scheduler saturation suspected. :rotating_light:

devon: saw it. avg 502s reported by gateway and a bunch of 504s from model pool. queue_depth metrics jumping.

sasha: putting quick summary here — we have queue_depth ~ 1200 on scheduler, avg_batch_wait_ms ~ 3200, tail latency > 6s, sudden tokenization CPU spike reported on a small subset of hosts.

mike: stacktrace-ish from one host:```
2026-03-15T12:07:02Z ERROR scheduler: accept failed: queue_depth=1243, wait_ms=3758
2026-03-15T12:07:04Z WARN tokenizer: tokenization-worker-3 CPU 98%
2026-03-15T12:07:05Z ERROR gateway: upstream 502 on /v1/generate (timeout)
```

lisa: customer-facing: multiple customers hitting 502s in US-West. Support already holding a few P1 chats. Need ETA and mitigation.

devon: oncall handoff — I'm on it but gonna escalate to sasha if mitigation requires changes to routing. Assigning to me for initial triage.

sasha: thanks. initial hypothesis: a recent model quantization change on pool-rtq-2 introduced an expensive path in tokenizer for certain Unicode sequences, causing long tokenization tasks that block batch slots (head-of-line blocking).

mike: confirming — logs show a tight correlation between requests with long input sequences containing emojis/rare scripts and tokenization CPU spikes.

incidents-bot: Paging devon -> devon acknowledged the page at 12:08.

devon: mitigation attempt 1: enable short-circuit for tokenization fallback on affected hosts (config flag: `tokenizer.fast_fallback=true`). Rolling to 3/6 hosts in pool-rtq-2.

sasha: good. while that rolls, can we drain long-waiting batches? Is there an eviction knob?

mike: there's a safe eviction: `scheduler.evict_threshold_ms=2500` — currently set to 10s. We can lower to 2500ms to prevent HOL. Will require careful coord with gateway to avoid request loss.

devon: proposing sequence: 1) set evict_threshold to 2500ms (soft eviction, return 429 to clients we can retry), 2) enable tokenizer.fast_fallback on remaining hosts, 3) route new incoming traffic to fallback model variant for 60m. Anyone object?

lisa: support needs a short status line for customers — can we confirm whether fallback model will preserve API contract?

sasha: fallback model variant is same API but slightly smaller (same interface, different model_id: `redwood/ft-small-v1`). Quality should be fine for 60m. We'll mark it in headers.

ops-bot: NOTE: applying change `scheduler.evict_threshold_ms=2500` via ops pipeline. Confirm with :thumbsup: to proceed.

mike: :thumbsup: proceed. I'll watch errors and request success.

incidents-bot: ACTION TAKEN: evict_threshold lowered to 2500ms at 12:12.

devon: evicting long-waiting batches now, returning retryable 429 for ~1100 requests stuck >2500ms. Gateway will surface 429 to clients.

lisa: copy — telling customers: "We've throttled long-running in-flight requests to stabilize the service; retrying should succeed. We're routing new requests to a fallback model; no data loss."

sasha: enabling tokenizer.fast_fallback on remaining 3 hosts now.

mike: after changes: queue_depth dropped from ~1200 to ~200 within 90s. 5xx rate down from 12% -> 1.8% in US-West. Tail latency improving.

devon: good improvement. I'm keeping the page but will stand down once stabilized and support confirms customer impact reduced.

incidents-bot: ALERT: New error trend detected — 5xx at 1.9% (was 12%). Monitoring for recurrence.

lisa: support reports significant reduction in customer complaints. A few clients still seeing retries but OK.

sasha: root cause notes for postmortem: a tokenizer regression in quantized model variant caused excessive CPU per-token for certain inputs; that created head-of-line blocking in scheduler batches leading to gateway timeouts and 5xx.

mike: follow-up runbook updates: add heuristics to detect tokenization hot inputs, add per-request tokenization timeout, and ensure scheduler has more aggressive soft-evict default during spikes.

devon: next steps: keep fallback model routing for 60m, monitor, prepare rollback if any new regressions, create postmortem ticket with RCA and timeline. I'll create the ticket and assign to eng-ml + eng-runtime.

lisa: communicated to customers at 12:28 PT: "Service stabilized; if you still see errors please contact support with request-id header."

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> under monitoring. Will update when fully resolved.

sasha: adding one more note — we should add a traffic-weighted canary for tokenizer changes; don't roll quantized tokenizer change to >10% traffic without synthetic load test.

mike: logged metrics snapshot for postmortem:```
pre-change: queue_depth=1188, 5xx_rate=0.12, avg_batch_wait_ms=3240
post-change: queue_depth=194, 5xx_rate=0.018, avg_batch_wait_ms=420
```

devon: standing down at 12:34; leaving monitoring handover to sasha for the next 45m. Thanks everyone. :heart:

incidents-bot: Thread closed for active paging. Please link postmortem ticket when created."
